answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-bonded, work-proven identity: each agent locks a refundable bond and earns spending rights only after completing verifiable jobs checked by independent peers. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust, with a low rate limit, and must survive a tide of audits before its quota rises. Creating a thousand hollow identities costs a thousand bonds plus compute and time to pass real audits, while one honest agent pays once and reuses its proven record. Cheating forfeits the bond and burns its history, so forgery scales in cost but honesty does not.
